name: ISS
desc: The International Space Station. 400km above, always occupied since 2000.

name: Tiangong CSS
desc: China's national space station. A new permanence in orbit.

name: Hubble Space Telescope
desc: Launched blind. Given sight by astronauts. Changed everything.

name: NOAA-19
desc: Fell 1.5 metres onto a factory floor during assembly. Nobody had installed the bolts.

name: Terra
desc: NASA's flagship Earth observer. Watching the planet change since 1999.

name: Aqua
desc: Studying Earth's water cycle. Every ocean, every cloud.

name: Sentinel-2A
desc: ESA's land monitor. Free imagery for the entire planet, every five days.

name: Landsat 8
desc: Fifty years of continuous Earth observation. The longest environmental record from space.

name: CryoSat-2
desc: Measuring ice loss with centimetre precision. The numbers are not reassuring.

name: Swarm-A
desc: Mapping Earth's magnetic field. The invisible architecture that makes life possible.

name: Vanguard 1
desc: The oldest human-made object still in orbit. Launched 1958. Will remain for 600 more years.

name: OSCAR-7
desc: Amateur radio satellite. Died 1981. Came back to life in 2002. Used daily ever since.

name: Jason-3
desc: Measuring sea surface height with millimetre precision. The oceans are rising.

name: Starlink-30
desc: One of thousands. The constellation that changed what the night sky looks like.

name: Starlink-31
desc: One of thousands. Astronomers are still deciding how they feel about this.

name: ICESat-2
desc: Fires 10,000 laser pulses per second at the ice sheets. Measuring their disappearance with centimetre precision.

name: CloudSat
desc: Flies in tight formation with four other satellites, 15 seconds apart. Has been looking straight down at clouds since 2006.

name: CALIPSO
desc: Shoots a laser at aerosols and smoke. Mapped the Saharan dust that fertilises the Amazon.

name: Aquarius / SAC-D
desc: Mapped ocean salinity for the first time from space. Retired 2015, still up there.

name: Envisat
desc: ESA's largest Earth observation satellite. Went silent in 2012. Still orbiting.
